author: Arigenn
body:
Hello Avicus Community,

The senior staff team would like feedback from the community of Avicus, so we can strive towards becoming better senior staff members individually, and as a whole team. To do this, we need community members to submit feedback which will be given to us through a google form (https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1V-L-fSQqT9QdE1oN4HU1W1sybVfI5ET8iWYFQ-ZH8EA/viewform).

We hope you partake in giving feedback to us, and thank you in advance.

replies.author: Howsie
replies.body:
I know this isn't something I should get butthurt over but I'm going to rant about it anyway! 

1. You shouldn't be expecting your community to critique you ESPECIALLY to the extent of what you're asking (which from what I can tell is a few sentences to a paragraph)

2. As the leading members of the community asking others to critique you is a sign that you are unsure about your position. If you believe there are issues within your ranks, that is your responsibility, especially for a group of people who SHOULD have earned the position and have enough respect and their capability to do their job correctly. That responsibility certainly shouldn't fall to those who theoretically are the ones you're taking care of and dare I say it are 'below' you in terms of hierarchy and authority. 

3. Maybe less than 2% of active users would have good reasons to bash or praise the staff member and even if they did why would they take the time out of their day to write essays about each of you. The forums should be a chilled out place to talk about chilled out topics, not fill in surveys and critique things unnecessarily. 

On the topic of being chilled out by the way - have you noticed the user count nowadays? Maybe if we were at the height of popularity the insistence on conservative moderator practice and community management would be valid but it just isn't. Slim down the staff team and make sure they're aware their purpose isn't to impose, its to support.

Its late, I'm tired - If any or none of this makes sense, ask me to elaborate.

If I was a non-staff member, I would want a way to submit feedback that I had for the staff team. If you want feedback, it doesn't necessarily mean you are unsure about your position, and I think every member of the staff team currently can improve on feedback.

Feedback is a pretty important aspect to receive in my opinion, it pushes you to further improve yourself as in your role on the staff team, and I can say that I take my feedback seriously and have improved on feedback given to me in the past.

I'm sorry but I don't see how submitting a form for the community to give feedback will hurt anything on the forums community, and its does more help than harm.

replies.author: Howsie
replies.body:
What I would recommend, in terms of feedback, is having a centralised spot of the forum (which already exists) and make that the only and I mean ONLY place users can send feedback. Encourage the community to use it, have people in the staff team monitoring it, responding to/suggesting ideas in posts. I don't watch the forums that closely, but when I am on here there is always some sort of 'online survey' going on. That wouldn't be that big an issue if the surveys weren't do you like or dislike this thing & please now give an essay about why you dislike or like this thing. 

Feedback is important, I'm with you on that, but these sort of 'surveys' provokes the idea that something could be wrong. If people want to give feedback, push them towards a centralised area is pretty much the idea here. 

The other thing is the only time I tried doing a survey proved extremely useless as we had 300+ responses which no one really wanted to read through. Some ideas were taken on but realistically it was a waste of time.
